title: Audit Export (SIEM-ready) — Config API Outline (early sketch)
body:
Context
- This is an early control-plane API sketch for “SIEM-ready audit export (beta)”.
- Goal: destination CRUD, filter rule validation, and health/status endpoints that Console can use.
- Not final. Expect changes once delivery semantics + schema v1 lock.

Non-goals (for this doc)
- Worker/queue internal APIs
- Admin-only ops endpoints (pause worker globally, drain queue, etc.)
- Full “replay a time window” API (may become separate doc)

Key concepts (naming is still TBD)
- Workspace: customer tenant boundary in Redwood Console.
- Environment: {prod|staging|dev} (or more generally “logical environment”) within workspace. (Open question: do we support export-per-env at beta?)
- Destination: where to deliver audit events. Types: splunk_hec | datadog_logs | s3
- Filter rules: include/exclude criteria to reduce noise/cost.
- Delivery pipeline state: enabled/paused/degraded/disabled (exact enum TBD)

High-level control-plane model (draft)
- Destination belongs to: workspace_id + (optionally) environment
- Destination has:
  - type
  - credentials reference (secret id)
  - config (host/index/bucket/etc.)
  - filter
  - status: last_success_at, last_error_at, last_error_code, backlog_estimate, last_delivered_event_time

AuthZ / RBAC notes
- RBAC permission name candidates:
  - audit_export:read
  - audit_export:write
  - audit_export:send_test
  - audit_export:pause_resume
- Only workspace admins/security admins should have write/send_test.
- Audit log must record destination CRUD and filter changes (separate schema work).

API style decisions (tentative)
- REST over JSON.
- Prefer idempotent updates:
  - PUT for full replace (with revision token)
  - PATCH for partial updates
- Concurrency:
  - return “etag” or “revision” integer
  - client must send If-Match / revision on updates

Base path
- /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export

1) Destination CRUD

1.1 List destinations
GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations?environment=prod
Response 200:
{
  "destinations": [ {DestinationSummary}... ],
  "next_page_token": "..." (optional)
}

DestinationSummary (draft):
{
  "id": "dest_01H...",
  "name": "Security Splunk (prod)",
  "type": "splunk_hec",
  "environment": "prod",
  "state": "enabled",
  "created_at": "...",
  "updated_at": "...",
  "health": {
    "status": "healthy|degraded|error|paused|unknown",
    "last_success_at": "...",
    "last_attempt_at": "...",
    "last_error_code": "splunk_401|splunk_5xx|datadog_429|s3_access_denied|schema_validation|network|unknown",
    "backlog_estimate": "approx int as string?",
    "delivery_lag_seconds": "approx int as string?"
  }
}

Note: “health” might be too heavy for list; could return minimal fields + provide separate /health endpoint.

1.2 Get destination detail
GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
Response 200:
{
  "id": "dest_...",
  "revision": 17,
  "name": "...",
  "type": "splunk_hec",
  "environment": "prod",
  "state": "enabled",
  "filter": {FilterSpec},
  "config": {TypeSpecificConfig},
  "credentials": {CredentialRef},
  "health": {HealthDetail},
  "created_at": "...",
  "updated_at": "..."
}

Security note: credentials should NEVER return secrets. Only show reference metadata (e.g., created_at, last_rotated_at).

CredentialRef (draft):
{
  "secret_id": "sec_...",
  "kind": "splunk_hec_token|datadog_api_key|aws_iam_role|aws_access_key" (beta: likely token/key + IAM role),
  "last_rotated_at": "..." (optional)
}

1.3 Create destination
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations
Request:
{
  "name": "Security Splunk (prod)",
  "type": "splunk_hec",
  "environment": "prod",
  "state": "enabled", (optional; default disabled?)
  "filter": {FilterSpec},
  "config": {TypeSpecificConfig},
  "credentials": {CredentialCreateOrRef}
}
Response 201:
{ DestinationDetail }

CredentialCreateOrRef options (open question: do we allow passing raw secret values to CP API?)
Option A (preferred): Console sends secret to Secrets service; CP stores only secret_id.
- credentials: { "secret_id": "sec_..." }
Option B: CP endpoint accepts secret material and writes to secrets store.
- credentials: { "kind": "splunk_hec_token", "value": "***" }
Security/GRC likely prefers A to ensure consistent secret handling + auditing.

TypeSpecificConfig examples (draft)

Splunk HEC:
{
  "endpoint": "https://http-inputs-xxx.splunkcloud.com:8088",
  "hec_token_secret_id": "sec_...", (if using Option A)
  "index": "redwood_audit",
  "source": "redwood",
  "sourcetype": "redwood:audit:v1",
  "use_ack": true,
  "ack_poll_ms": 250,
  "max_batch_bytes": 950000,
  "max_batch_events": 500
}
Notes:
- Use ACK optional in beta; default true for Splunk Cloud? Needs ADR.

Datadog Logs intake:
{
  "site": "datadoghq.com|datadoghq.eu|us3.datadoghq.com" (TBD),
  "api_key_secret_id": "sec_...",
  "service": "redwood-inference",
  "tags": ["workspace:abc", "env:prod"]
}
Notes:
- DD expects JSON; we’ll send event as JSON with top-level fields.

S3 sink:
{
  "bucket": "company-audit-logs",
  "prefix": "redwood/audit/",
  "region": "us-east-1",
  "partition_format": "workspace_id=.../dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/",
  "format": "jsonl",
  "compression": "gzip",
  "sse": "SSE_S3|SSE_KMS",
  "kms_key_arn": "arn:aws:kms:..." (required if SSE_KMS),
  "iam_role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123:role/redwood-audit-export" (preferred),
  "object_max_mb": 128
}

1.4 Update destination (full replace)
PUT /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
Headers: If-Match: "17" (or body revision)
Request:
{ same shape as create but may omit immutable fields }
Response 200: DestinationDetail

Immutable fields candidates
- type (changing type == create new destination)
- workspace_id
- destination_id
Possibly immutable: environment (unclear; might allow moving env but complicates routing)

1.5 Patch destination (partial)
PATCH /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
Headers: If-Match: "17"
Request example:
{
  "state": "paused",
  "filter": {FilterSpec}
}

1.6 Delete destination
DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{destination_id}
Response 204.
Notes:
- Deleting should also disable worker routing; existing queued items for that destination:
  - Option 1: drop remaining with explicit “destination_deleted” metric
  - Option 2: retain for X hours for recovery (“undelete”) (probably too much for beta)
- Soft-delete might help avoid accidental loss; open question.

2) State / lifecycle endpoints

2.1 Pause/Resume convenience endpoints (optional)
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{id}:pause
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{id}:resume
Reason: simplifies Console flows; avoids ambiguous patch with state transitions.

State machine notes (draft)
- disabled: configured but not delivering
- enabled: delivering
- paused: explicitly paused by user (don’t retry until resumed)
- degraded: system determined (e.g., repeated 5xx, auth failures); still retrying with backoff
- error: hard failure (e.g., invalid config, repeated schema violations) requiring user action

Open question: “degraded vs error” might be too subtle for beta. Could have:
- enabled, paused, disabled; plus health.status indicates degraded/error.

3) Filter validation API

3.1 Validate filter (standalone)
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/filters:validate
Request:
{ "filter": {FilterSpec}, "destination_type": "splunk_hec" (optional) }
Response 200:
{
  "valid": true,
  "warnings": ["..."],
  "normalized_filter": {FilterSpec}
}
Response 400:
{
  "valid": false,
  "errors": [
    {"path": "filter.event_types[2]", "code": "unknown_event_type", "message": "..."},
    {"path": "filter.actors.include[0]", "code": "invalid_actor_format", "message": "..."}
  ]
}

Why standalone validation?
- Console needs immediate feedback before saving
- Also used by “test delivery” to ensure we can accept the filter

FilterSpec (draft; expect changes once audit schema v1 taxonomy final)
{
  "mode": "allowlist|blocklist" (open question: do we support both? maybe allowlist only for beta),
  "event_types": {
    "include": ["auth.login", "rbac.role_grant", "api_key.rotate"],
    "exclude": ["*"?]
  },
  "actors": {
    "include": ["user:123", "service_account:456"],
    "exclude": []
  },
  "resources": {
    "include": ["model:*", "workspace:abc"],
    "exclude": []
  },
  "environments": ["prod"],
  "ip": {
    "include_cidrs": ["203.0.113.0/24"],
    "exclude_cidrs": []
  },
  "regions": {
    "include": ["us-east-1"],
    "exclude": []
  }
}

Notes / simplifications for beta
- Might drop ip/regions in beta to reduce complexity (or keep but validation-only).
- Actors/resources patterns: do we allow globs? Regex? Probably simple prefix + “*” suffix only.
- If allowlist-only: filter = { "event_types": ["..."] ... } (simple arrays).

4) Test delivery / credential verification

4.1 Send test event
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{id}:test
Request:
{
  "mode": "connectivity|end_to_end",
  "sample_event_type": "audit_export.test" (or use fixed internal type)
}
Response 200:
{
  "delivered": true,
  "sink_response": "Splunk code=200 ackId=...",
  "event_id": "evt_test_...",
  "delivered_at": "..."
}
Response 424 or 502 (TBD):
{
  "delivered": false,
  "error_code": "splunk_401|datadog_403|s3_access_denied|network_timeout|invalid_tls|throttled",
  "message": "...",
  "retry_after_seconds": "..." (optional)
}

Notes
- Should not enqueue into normal queue for test unless we want consistent codepath.
  - Option A: synchronous connector send (fast feedback)
  - Option B: enqueue with priority and poll status (more realistic but UX harder)
- Test must emit audit event “audit_export.test_sent” (internal-only?)

4.2 Verify credentials without creating destination (optional)
POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/credentials:verify
Probably unnecessary if create + test covers it.

5) Health / status endpoints

5.1 Destination health detail
GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/destinations/{id}/health
Response:
{
  "status": "healthy|degraded|error|paused|unknown",
  "status_reason": "...",
  "last_success_at": "...",
  "last_attempt_at": "...",
  "last_delivered_event_time": "..." (this is the event’s occurred_at),
  "backlog_estimate": "12345",
  "delivery_lag_seconds": "180",
  "recent_errors": [
    "2025-01-28T19:33Z splunk_5xx: upstream timeout",
    "2025-01-28T19:35Z splunk_5xx: upstream timeout"
  ],
  "counters_15m": {
    "sent": "...",
    "failed": "...",
    "retried": "...",
    "dropped": "..." (should be 0; only if we intentionally drop)
  }
}

Important: This “counters_15m” object is nested if we implement literally. For this sketch, just noting desired data. Actual API might flatten or return arrays.

5.2 Workspace-level overview (for Console landing page)
GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit-export/health?environment=prod
Response:
{
  "overall_status": "healthy|degraded|error|disabled",
  "destinations": [ {DestinationSummary or smaller} ]
}

Open question: Do we want workspace-level health endpoint vs relying on list+health per destination? Likely yes for performance and consistent status rules.

6) Error model (draft)
Common error response:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_argument|permission_denied|not_found|conflict|rate_limited|upstream_error",
    "message": "Human readable",
    "details": ["path=... code=... msg=..."]
  },
  "request_id": "req_..."
}

7) Pagination & sorting
- List destinations probably small; pagination optional.
- Add support for sort=created_at desc.

8) Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we scope destinations by environment?
  - Pro: fewer surprises; customers can separate prod vs staging
  - Con: more config complexity; does our audit event stream include environment reliably?

- Exactly what’s allowed in filter for beta?
  - If we include IP/region, we must validate and clearly document semantics.
  - We should ensure “empty filter” has safe default (likely minimal allowlist rather than “everything”? PM decision).

- Secrets handling:
  - Strong preference: Console uses secrets API, CP stores secret_id.
  - Need to confirm how Private deployments handle secrets store (K8s secret vs external KMS).

- Health accuracy:
  - backlog_estimate might be approximate and stale; define update intervals.
  - last_delivered_event_time vs last_success_at: both useful; define clearly.

- Destination uniqueness constraints:
  - Can customer create multiple Splunk destinations for same env? Probably yes.
  - Should we allow only one destination per type per env? Probably no; partners might want two indexes.

- Deletion semantics / data retention:
  - When a destination is deleted, do we purge queued events for it or retain until TTL?

- Idempotency keys for POST create:
  - Should support Idempotency-Key header to prevent duplicates when Console retries.

- “Normalized filter” response:
  - If we rewrite/normalize patterns (e.g., trim spaces, canonicalize event types), we should return it so Console shows what’s applied.

9) Alternative shapes (recorded for discussion)

Alt A: Single endpoint for CRUD + actions
- POST /destinations/{id}:action with {"action":"pause"}
Pros: fewer endpoints
Cons: less REST-y; harder to authorize action-specific permissions

Alt B: Nested sub-resources per type
- /destinations/splunk
- /destinations/datadog
Pros: type-specific schemas cleaner
Cons: more endpoints; harder for Console list + generic UX

Alt C: Put filter as separate resource
- /destinations/{id}/filter
Pros: separate permissions (let security team manage filters without touching creds?)
Cons: added complexity

10) Next steps
- Align with Console team on minimal endpoints needed for beta flows (create, edit, pause, test, view health).
- Confirm filter shape with Security Eng + schema v1 taxonomy owner.
- Decide on “health in list response” vs separate call.
- Draft request/response JSON schema definitions (OpenAPI) once settled.

Notes to self
- Keep API compatible across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; avoid dependencies on internal-only infra.
- Ensure any config changes are themselves audit-logged (meta!)
- Design for at-least-once semantics messaging; duplicates possible downstream; health should not imply “exactly once”.
